sections.h2: Where is Tigard, Oregon, and how is the city laid out?
sections.html:
Tigard is a Washington County city that sits south of Beaverton and north of Tualatin in the Portland metro area. The Census Bureau lists 12.67 square miles of land for the city, and the 2020 census counted every resident as living in an urban area.

Interstate 5 runs along the eastern edge. Oregon Route 217 ends at I-5 inside the city, Highway 99W cuts through it, Oregon Route 210 forms part of the northern boundary, and Oregon Route 141 follows Boones Ferry Road and Hall Boulevard. A seller here is rarely more than a few minutes from a major road, which helps when buyers and appraisers compare the house with others nearby.

Tigard has ZIP codes 97223 (north of McDonald Street) and 97224 (the southern half). Fire and medical response comes from Tualatin Valley Fire and Rescue.

sections.h2: How did Tigard grow from a farm community into a city of more than 50,000?
sections.html:
Tigard grew slowly for a century and then very fast. The Tigard family, led by Wilson M. Tigard, arrived in the East Butte area in 1852. The settlement was called Tigardville from 1886, and the railroad shortened the name to Tigard in 1907 so mail would not be confused with Wilsonville.

The Oregon Electric Railway reached town in 1910 and electricity followed in 1911. Tigard incorporated in 1961 with an estimated 1,084 people. Census counts then climbed from 6,499 in 1970 to 14,799 in 1980, 29,344 in 1990 and 42,249 in 2000, before reaching 54,539 in 2020.

That curve means a large share of Tigard houses were probably built in the 1970s, 1980s and 1990s. Homes of that age often carry older roofs, windows and sewer laterals, which is one reason owners here weigh repair costs before deciding how to sell. The city also appears in legal history: Dolan v. City of Tigard (1994) produced the U.S. Supreme Court's “rough proportionality” test for development conditions. The John Tigard House, built in 1880, has been on the National Register of Historic Places since 1979.

sections.h2: What do Census Bureau figures say about Tigard homes and households?
sections.html:
Tigard is a mix of owner-occupied and rented homes, with owners in the majority. The table below uses the Census Bureau’s 2020 to 2024 survey data for the city.

The median value is a survey figure for owner-occupied homes, not a price for any one house. A property that needs a new roof or has been a rental for years can sit well below it, and that gap is where many sellers start asking about as-is options.

sections.h2: Which parts of Tigard are changing, and why does it matter to a seller?
sections.html:
Three areas get most of the city’s planning attention. If your house is in one of them, ask the city what the current zoning allows before you pick a sale route.

  • Downtown Main Street. It grew after the 1910 railroad and still anchors the older part of town.
  • Tigard Triangle. About 550 acres in the northeast corner, bounded by Highway 99W, Highway 217 and I-5. Voters approved a tax increment financing district in May 2017, and the council rezoned most of the area to a Triangle Mixed-Use zone. The city’s own page lists vacant lots, flooding, congestion and broken sewer lines among the barriers, and a 2016 study scored its walkability at 33 out of 100 against 66 for downtown.
  • Washington Square Regional Center. Metro designates it one of eight regional centers, and it reaches nearly a mile in each direction from the mall. Tigard adopted code updates for it on April 23, 2024, effective May 23, 2024.

Bull Mountain, the hill area west of the city, is unincorporated. Voters approved annexing it in 2004, but residents there have rejected annexation and litigation has continued. Whether an address is inside city limits changes which permits and code rules apply, so check the address before assuming.

sections.h2: What schools, jobs and transit tie Tigard buyers to the area?
sections.html:
Most of Tigard is in the Tigard-Tualatin School District, which began as East Butte School District 23 in 1875 and now enrolls about 12,625 students. It runs 11 elementary schools, three middle schools (Fowler, Hazelbrook and Twality) and two high schools, Tigard High and Tualatin High. A small northwestern slice of the city is in the Beaverton School District.

Retail and services employ many residents. A 2014 employer list put Capital One Services first with 861 employees, followed by the school district at 779, Nordstrom at 422 and Macy’s at 404. Washington Square mall and the northern part of Bridgeport Village are both in or at the edge of Tigard. Companies headquartered here include Consumer Cellular, Gerber Legendary Blades and NuScale Power.

For commuting, TriMet buses serve the city, the WES commuter rail stops at the Tigard Transit Center, and Washington Square Transit Center is the second hub. A proposed Southwest Corridor MAX extension failed at the ballot in November 2020, so no light rail line is coming to Tigard under that plan.

sections.h2: How do Washington County property taxes work for a Tigard seller?
sections.html:
Washington County bills Tigard property owners on a July 1 to June 30 tax year, with three due dates. For 2025 to 2026 they were November 17, 2025, February 17, 2026 and May 15, 2026. Paying in full by the first date earns a 3% discount, and paying two-thirds earns 2%.

The county mailed about 207,000 statements that year, totaling $1.742 billion, up 11.7%. It reports 360 tax code areas and 64 local taxing districts, and value appeals were open until December 31, 2025.

The state side matters at closing. Oregon property tax becomes a lien on July 1, interest runs at 1.333% per month once a payment is late, and a change of owner after July 1 may not show on the fall statement, so confirm the amount with the tax collector. Unpaid taxes are a common reason sellers start looking for faster routes.

sections.h2: Does Washington County charge a transfer tax when a Tigard house sells?
sections.html:
Yes. Washington County charges $1 for every $1,000 of the selling price on a sale, quitclaim, contract for sale or other transfer of title. On a $500,000 sale that works out to $500.

The county says liability for the tax is between purchaser and seller, so the purchase contract should say who pays. The tax must be paid, or an exemption filed, within 15 days of recording, and a late penalty applies after that.

The county lists exemptions, including:

  • deeds in lieu of foreclosure and court-ordered transfers
  • a trustee’s deed from foreclosure
  • transfers by gift, devise or inheritance
  • transfers between spouses under a divorce or separation order

An inherited Tigard house passed to an heir may qualify, but the later sale by that heir is a normal sale and is taxed.

sections.h2: What must a Tigard seller disclose under Oregon law?
sections.html:
Oregon requires most sellers of homes with one to four dwelling units to hand each buyer who makes a written offer a signed seller’s property disclosure statement (ORS 105.465). The buyer then has five business days after delivery to revoke the offer in writing, and a seller who never delivers the form leaves that right open until it is cut off by closing (ORS 105.475).

ORS 105.470 excludes some sellers, including court-appointed personal representatives and trustees, and lenders selling after foreclosure or a deed in lieu. A Tigard family selling a parent’s house through an estate may fall in that group, which can shorten the paperwork.

sections.h2: How does a cash sale of a Tigard house work?
sections.html:
A cash sale replaces the listing, showings and lender approval with a direct purchase of the house in its current condition. You describe the property, the buyer reviews it and makes an offer, and if you accept, a title company in Washington County opens escrow and handles the deed and recording.

Cash does not remove the Oregon steps above. The disclosure form, the county transfer tax and the property tax proration still apply, and you can ask the title officer to show each line before you sign. Compare any offer with what a listing would net after repairs, agent fees, carrying costs and time on market.

faqs.q: Is Tigard in Washington County or Clackamas County?
faqs.a: Tigard is in Washington County. Washington County bills the property tax and collects the county transfer tax on a sale.

faqs.q: What is the Washington County transfer tax rate on a Tigard sale?
faqs.a: The rate is $1 per $1,000 of the selling price. Liability is shared between buyer and seller by agreement, and payment or an exemption filing is due within 15 days of recording.

faqs.q: When are property taxes due in Tigard?
faqs.a: Washington County uses three due dates each year in November, February and May, with 3% off for paying in full by the November date. For 2025 to 2026 the dates were November 17, February 17 and May 15.

faqs.q: Can I sell a Tigard house that has repairs or code problems?
faqs.a: Yes. A seller who completes the Oregon disclosure form has to describe known problems on it, and a buyer who gets that form has five business days to revoke the offer. A cash buyer can purchase the house as it stands, so repairs do not have to come first.

faqs.q: Which school district covers my Tigard house?
faqs.a: Most of Tigard is in the Tigard-Tualatin School District. A small northwestern part of the city is in the Beaverton School District, so check the address with the district.

faqs.q: Does the Tigard Triangle affect my home sale?
faqs.a: It can. The city rezoned most of the Triangle to a mixed-use zone in 2017, so a property there may have different allowed uses than a typical neighborhood lot. Ask the city planning office what applies to your parcel.
